_doc: Spatial-provenance manifest. Enforced by .claude/scripts/check-layer-colocation.sh (wired into ./dev.sh --check-encoding and encoding-loop.yml CI). Four gates: (1) every served web/public/maps/*.geojson must be declared in `layers`; (2) any `comparisons` head-to-head must be co-located (bbox IoU >= min_iou); (3) each reach's imaged extent must not be a TRUNCATION of the declared reach: the center-offset of imaged-vs-defined bbox must be <= offset_threshold OR the reach carries a discrepancy_ack (raw IoU is reported but does not gate, since a narrow river centered in a tall AOI has low IoU yet is not truncated); (4) a reach whose NAME implies a morphology (arroyo/wash/...) that conflicts with its declared `morphology` must carry a discrepancy_ack. Rationale + the failure this prevents: docs/2026-08-21-reach-provenance-gap.md.

malpais.name: Malpais Arroyo–San Juan
malpais.discrepancy_ack: RETRACTED 2026-08-21: the imaged windows cover only the southern San Juan valley; the defined reach extends ~6 km north (up the wash) and the arroyo was never imaged or scored. Name says 'Arroyo' but the geometry is river-dominated. See docs/2026-08-21-reach-provenance-gap.md.

kirtland.name: Kirtland — San Juan mainstem
kirtland.note: Reviewed 2026-08-21 (the 'Malpais treatment'): the low bbox IoU (0.395) is a NARROW-CORRIDOR artifact, not a truncation. The imaged band is CENTERED in the AOI (center-offset 0.02) and spans the full E-W river length — it is the San Juan mainstem through the middle of a tall rectangular AOI; the N/S extremes are upland with no riparian. Unlike Malpais (offset 0.21, missing the northern arroyo), Kirtland was NOT truncated. The 0.845 river-reach transfer score stands. The extent gate now flags center-offset, not raw IoU, so this no longer trips.

web/public/maps/truth_malpais.geojson.note: NMRipMap expert riparian over the imaged San Juan-valley extent

web/public/maps/reach-malpais-rf.geojson.note: LORO-scored RF (train on the other reaches, predict Malpais); fires only in a small eastern pocket — the RF collapses reach-wide (AUC 0.56), unlike FM (0.89)

web/public/maps/fm_malpais.geojson.note: OlmoEarth over the imaged San Juan-valley extent

comparisons.name: bloomfield-truth-rf-fm
comparisons.note: The honest RF-vs-FM head-to-head: expert truth + RF + FM, genuinely co-located.

_selftest_note: The former malpais rf-vs-fm self-test was premised on a MISLOCATION reading (rf ~5 km from fm). On re-verification (2026-08-21, bar reproduced + NMRipMap has no wash labels) that reading was superseded: RF and FM cover the SAME reach — the RF simply UNDER-FIRES (near-chance, AUC 0.56, fires only in an eastern pocket) while FM tracks the corridor (0.89). Low RF-vs-FM overlap here is a real model-quality finding, not a provenance error, so it is no longer a 'must-flag' self-test. The co-location gate still self-checks on real comparisons.
